mainTopic: The rules of קנין אגב: piling, required wording, mixed deals, and paying for everything
overview: This amud is about קנין אגב: acquiring movable items together with land. First the גמרא asks whether the movables must be piled on the land. Proofs from רבן גמליאל's tithes and from רב הונא's third type of שטר are each pushed away. A ברייתא then shows that a שטר is just like any movable, so the גמרא concludes that piling is not needed. Next it rules that the seller must say both 'אגב' and 'קני.' Two more questions follow. A field sold with movables given as a gift is proven from רבן גמליאל's words to יהושע. A field to one person with movables to another is not proven, because of how רבי עקיבא's part is explained. Finally, רבא rules that a buyer paying with money acquires only as much as he paid for, and a ברייתא comparing כסף, שטר and חזקה begins to support him; it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל rents out the place of his tithes
steps.stepSummary: The end of the story about רבן גמליאל, who gave his מעשרות together with 'their place,' is used to prove that items must be piled on the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: …is given to יהושע, and its place is rented to him. And another tenth that I will measure in the future is given to עקיבא בן יוסף, so that he can acquire it for the poor, and its place is rented to him. Learn from this: we require the items to be piled on the land!
steps.whatsHappening: We are finishing the story of רבן גמליאל giving away his מעשרות through the land they sat on. The גמרא then concludes from it that items must be piled on the land to be acquired with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל did not just give the land. He specifically rented out 'its place,' the exact spot where the produce was lying. The גמרא reads this as a sign that the land only carries the produce along if the produce is actually sitting on it.

keyTerms.meaning: its place: the spot where the produce is lying
rented
a tenth (a tithe)
learn from this: the גמרא is drawing a conclusion
piled up on the land

phrases.english: is given to Yehoshua,
phrases.notes: We're joining רבן גמליאל mid-sentence: the first tithe of his produce goes to רבי יהושע, who was a לוי.

phrases.english: and its place is rented to him.
And another tenth that I will measure in the future
phrases.notes: This second tenth is the tithe for the poor.

phrases.english: is given to Akiva ben Yosef,
so that he can acquire it on behalf of the poor,
and its place is rented to him.
Learn from this: we require the items to be piled on it!

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ בָּעֵינַן צְבוּרִים בַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the source text started earlier on the daf and draws the proof from it.
steps.raayaObject: That movable items must be piled on the land to be acquired with it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבן גמליאל specifically rented out 'its place,' the exact spot of the produce.

steps.title: He only wanted to save them the trouble
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed away: רבן גמליאל gave 'its place' only so the חכמים would not have to carry the produce elsewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, so that he would not trouble them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from רבן גמליאל. He mentioned 'its place' for convenience, not because the law demands it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The produce was already lying in a certain spot. Giving them that exact spot saved רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא from moving it. So the story tells us nothing about whether piling is legally required.

keyTerms.meaning: it is different there
to trouble them, to make them work

phrases.english: It is different there,
so that he would not trouble them.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects this proof completely; the question is settled later, in step 8.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The detail 'its place' had a practical reason, so it is not a legal requirement.

steps.title: רב teaches two kinds of documents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new proof with רב's teaching about two ways of giving a field and a שטר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבא בר יצחק said in the name of רב: There are two kinds of documents. If one says, 'Acquire this field for so-and-so and write him the document,' he can retract about the document but not about the field. If he says, 'On condition that you write him the document,' he can retract about both the document and the field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new attempt to solve the question with 'תא שמע.' This step is setting up the next move: רב's list of two documents is about to be expanded to three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first wording, the field is given right away and the שטר is just an extra, so only the שטר can be cancelled. In the second wording, the whole gift depends on the שטר being written, so until then he can cancel everything. The real proof will come from the third type added in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: documents, deeds
acquire (on someone's behalf)
can retract, can take it back
on condition that

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for the proof in these two cases. They are the background. The proof comes from the third case in the next step.

phrases.english: Come and hear,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רָבָא בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: as Rava bar Yitzchak said that Rav said:
There are two kinds of documents:
'Acquire this field for so-and-so
and write him the document' —
he can retract regarding the document,
but he cannot retract regarding the field.
'On condition that you write him the document' —
he can retract both regarding the document and regarding the field.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רָבָא בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, the גמרא opens a new source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Acquire and write' lets him retract only the שטר; 'on condition that you write' lets him retract both.

steps.title: רב הונא adds a third document
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says there is a third type: a שטר the seller wrote in advance, which is acquired together with the land wherever it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חייא בר אבין said in the name of רב הונא: There are three kinds of documents. Two are the ones we said. The other: if the seller wrote the document first, as we learned, 'We write a document for the seller even though the buyer is not with him.' Once the buyer takes possession of the land, the document is acquired wherever it is.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא adds a third case to רב's list. When a seller prepared the שטר ahead of time, the buyer gets the שטר the moment he takes the land, even if the שטר is somewhere else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He supports the idea of writing a שטר in advance with a משנה that lets a seller have a שטר written without the buyer present. The key words are 'wherever it is': the שטר is acquired through the land without sitting on it. This is what the גמרא will use as its proof.

keyTerms.meaning: the other one
went ahead, did it first
took possession (חזקה)
wherever it is

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: And Rav Chiyya bar Avin said that Rav Huna said:
There are three kinds of documents.
Two are the ones we said;
the other one:

phrases.aramaic: אִם קָדַם מוֹכֵר וְכָתַב לוֹ אֶת הַשְּׁטָר,
phrases.english: if the seller went ahead and wrote him the document,
like what we learned:
We write a document for the seller

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לוֹקֵחַ עִמּוֹ.
phrases.english: even though the buyer is not with him.
Once he takes possession of the land from him —
the document is acquired wherever it is.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: שְׁלֹשָׁה שְׁטָרוֹת הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands רב's list from step 3 with a third case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שטר the seller wrote in advance is acquired along with the land wherever it is.

steps.title: Proof that piling is not needed
steps.stepSummary: Since the שטר is acquired 'wherever it is,' the גמרא concludes that items do not need to be piled on the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: we do not require the items to be piled on it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws its conclusion from רב הונא's third case. Things can be acquired along with land even when they are not on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שטר is a movable item, and it was acquired through the land without being on the land. So this seems to prove the opposite of what step 1 tried to prove.

keyTerms.meaning: we do not require

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ לָא בָּעֵינַן צְבוּרִים בַּהּ!
phrases.english: Learn from this: we do not require the items to be piled on it!

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ לָא בָּעֵינַן צְבוּרִים בַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the proof from רב הונא's third case.
steps.raayaObject: That movable items do not need to be piled on the land.
steps.raayaSupportSource: 'The document is acquired wherever it is' in רב הונא's statement.

steps.title: A document is the bridle of the land
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed away: a שטר is special because it is tied to the land like a bridle, so it is not like other movables.
steps.simpleTranslation: A document is different, because it is the bridle of the land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from the שטר. A שטר about the land is so connected to it that it goes with the land automatically.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as a bridle is how you lead an animal, the שטר is how you hold onto the land. Because it is like part of the land, it does not need to sit on it. Ordinary movables have no such connection, so this answer limits the proof to a שטר. The next step challenges this answer.

keyTerms.meaning: a bridle, a halter
land

steps.whatToRemember: For now, both proofs seem to fail: רבן גמליאל's 'its place' was just to save effort, and a שטר seems special as 'the bridle of the land.' Steps 7 and 8 overturn the second rejection and conclude that piling is not needed.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that a שטר is 'the bridle of the land' sets the שטר apart as closely tied to the land, unlike ordinary movables.

phrases.english: A document is different,
for it is the bridle of the land.
phrases.notes: Like a bridle leads an animal, the שטר is how you hold onto the land, so it counts as tied to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי שְׁטָר דְּאַפְסֵירָא דְאַרְעָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits רב הונא's case to a שטר only, so no general rule can be learned from it.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A שטר is uniquely tied to the land, unlike other movables.

steps.title: The document case is linked to the משנה about all movables
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the previous דחיה. The ברייתא about the שטר itself says 'this is what we learned in the משנה' about movables acquired with land, so the שטר is not a special case.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught about this: 'This is what we learned in the משנה: property without a guarantee is acquired together with property that has a guarantee, through money, a document, or taking possession!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the idea that a שטר is special. The ברייתא itself connects the שטר case to the general משנה about all movables.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 claimed a שטר is unique because it is tied to the land 'like a bridle.' But the ברייתא says the שטר case is simply an example of the משנה's general rule about movables. So a שטר must follow the same rules as any other movable item.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught about this very case
Property with no guarantee: movable items, which cannot back a loan
Property with a guarantee: land, which backs a loan
Acquiring by taking possession or doing an act of ownership

phrases.english: But it was taught about this:
phrases.notes: 'This' means the case of the document that is acquired together with the land wherever it is.

phrases.english: This is what we learned:
Property that does not serve as a guarantee

phrases.aramaic: נִקְנִין עִם נְכָסִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם אַחְרָיוּת
phrases.english: is acquired together with property that serves as a guarantee
through money, through a document, and through taking possession!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא עֲלַהּ קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the דחיה of step 6, which said a שטר is a special case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 6 that a שטר is different from other movables because it is tied to the land.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא presents the שטר case as an example of the משנה's general rule for all movables. So the שטר cannot be a special exception.

steps.title: Conclusion: movables do not need to be piled on the land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that movables acquired along with land do not need to be piled on that land.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from it: we do not require the items to be piled on the land. Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 6 has been answered, so the proof from step 5 stands. The גמרא firmly concludes that the movables do not have to be on the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שטר is a regular movable, and it is acquired 'wherever it is.' So any movable can be acquired together with land even if it is somewhere else. The repeated 'שמע מינה' signals that the גמרא accepts this as settled.

keyTerms.meaning: Piled up on the land
Learn from it: a formula for drawing a conclusion

steps.whatToRemember: Movables acquired together with land do not need to be piled on that land.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: לָא בָּעֵינַן צְבוּרִים בָּהּ,
phrases.english: Learn from it: we do not require them to be piled on it,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the land being sold, and 'them' is the movable items.

phrases.english: learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: לָא בָּעֵינַן צְבוּרִים בָּהּ, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion now that the challenge in step 7 has succeeded.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In a קנין אגב, the movables do not need to be piled on the land.

steps.title: Must the seller say 'by means of'?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: for the movables to be acquired together with the land, must the seller say the word 'אגב'?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: do we require him to say 'by means of' or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the wording of this kind of קנין. This sets up the proof attempt in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know the movables can be acquired together with the land. Now the question is whether the seller must say that out loud, for example 'acquire these by means of the land.'

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them: an open question
By means of: saying the movables are acquired through the land

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
Do we require him to say 'by means of' or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מִי בָּעֵינַן ״אַגַּב״ אוֹ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about the same kind of קנין.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a קנין אגב require the seller to actually say 'אגב'?

steps.title: Proof from silence: the sources never mention 'by means of'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove that 'אגב' is not needed, because the ברייתות list all these cases without mentioning it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: they teach all these cases, and they do not teach 'by means of.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a proof that the word 'אגב' is not required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתות describe many cases of acquiring movables together with land, and none of them says the seller must say 'אגב.' The proof argues that if it were required, they would have mentioned it.

keyTerms.meaning: All these cases

phrases.english: Come and hear,
for they teach all these cases,
and they do not teach 'by means of.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּקָתָנֵי כֹּל הָנֵי, וְלָא קָתָנֵי אַגַּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attempts to answer the question of step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That the word 'אגב' is not required.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתות that list cases of קנין אגב without mentioning the word.

steps.title: They don't mention 'acquire' either
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The ברייתות also never say 'קני,' yet it is certainly required. So their silence about 'אגב' proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your reasoning, is 'acquire' taught? Rather, it doesn't work until he says 'acquire.' Here too, it doesn't work until he says 'by means of.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from silence by showing it would prove too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees the seller must say 'קני' ('acquire'), yet the ברייתות never mention it. So the ברייתות are not listing the required words at all. 'אגב' could likewise be required even though it is not mentioned.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning: shows that a line of thought proves too much
Acquire! The seller telling the buyer to acquire
Here too: applying the same logic

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not prove that 'אגב' is required. It only shows that the silence of the ברייתות is not a proof either way. The actual ruling comes in the next step.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning, is 'acquire' taught?
Rather, does it not work until he says 'acquire'?
phrases.notes: In other words: you surely agree he must say 'acquire,' even though it's not written.

phrases.english: Here too, it does not work until he says 'by means of.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְטַעְמָיךְ, ״קְנִי״ מִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from silence entirely.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתות also do not mention 'קני,' which is certainly required. So they are not listing the required words, and their silence about 'אגב' means nothing.

steps.title: The final ruling on piling, 'by means of,' and 'acquire'
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה: the movables do not need to be piled on the land, but the seller must say both 'אגב' and 'קני.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: piling we do not require; 'by means of' and 'acquire' we do require.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical bottom line for this kind of קנין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This combines both discussions. From step 8, piling is not needed. On wording, the הלכה requires the seller to say both 'אגב' and 'קני.'

keyTerms.meaning: And the הלכה is: introduces the practical ruling

steps.whatToRemember: For a קנין אגב: the movables need not be on the land, but the seller must say 'אגב' and 'קני.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical rule for selling or giving movables along with land.

phrases.english: And the halakha is:
piled on the land: we do not require,
'by means of' and 'acquire': we do require.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא: צְבוּרִים – לָא בָּעֵינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final ruling after the proof in step 10 was rejected.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: No piling is needed, but both 'אגב' and 'קני' must be said.

steps.title: A field sold, with movables given as a gift
steps.stepSummary: A new question: if the field is sold but the movables are a gift, can the movables still be acquired together with the field?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: a field given as a sale and movables given as a gift, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens another new question about a mixed deal. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we pictured both the land and the movables being transferred in the same way. Here the two are transferred in different ways, one sold and one given free. Can the קנין on the field still carry the gift along with it?

keyTerms.meaning: A sale
A gift
What is the law?

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
A field as a sale and movables as a gift, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: שָׂדֶה בְּמֶכֶר וּמְטַלְטְלִין בְּמַתָּנָה מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about a different kind of קנין אגב case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a קנין אגב work when the land is sold and the movables are given as a gift?

steps.title: Proof from רבן גמליאל's tithe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבן גמליאל, who gave the tithe as a gift and rented out its place, as proof that the mixed deal works.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'The tenth that I will measure out in the future is given to יהושע, and its place is rented to him.' Learn from this!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the earlier story of רבן גמליאל to answer the new question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that story the tithe was a gift, and the land it sat on was rented out, which is like a sale. Since the tithe was transferred through renting its place, a gift of movables can be acquired along with land that is transferred for payment. The גמרא does not reject this proof, so it answers the question of step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: A tenth: the tithe from the produce
Rented

phrases.english: Come and hear:
'The tenth that I will measure out in the future,'
phrases.notes: This is what רבן גמליאל said, from the story the סוגיא discussed earlier.

phrases.english: 'is given to Yehoshua,'
'and its place is rented to him,'
learn from this!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: עִישּׂוּר שֶׁאֲנִי עָתִיד לָמוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attempts to answer the question in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That movables given as a gift can be acquired along with land transferred for payment.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבן גמליאל gave the tithe as a gift and rented its place to יהושע.

steps.title: The place was rented for the tithe itself
steps.stepSummary: A new question is asked: can the field go to one person and the movables to another? A proof is brought from רבן גמליאל's words to רבי עקיבא, and then rejected: 'rented' means rented for the sake of the tithe, so the land and the tithe both went to the poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: The question was: what if the field goes to one person and the movables go to another? The proof was רבן גמליאל, who gave the tithe to רבי עקיבא for the poor and rented its place to him. The גמרא answers: what does 'rented' mean? Rented for the tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question about giving the field to one person and the movables to another, and tries to prove it from רבן גמליאל's gift to רבי עקיבא. It then knocks down that proof: the place was rented only so the tithe could rest there for the poor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof worked only if the land went to רבי עקיבא while the tithe went to the poor. If the land was rented on behalf of the tithe, then land and tithe went to the same side, the poor. So this is not a case of 'field to one, movables to another.'

keyTerms.meaning: rented
rented for the tithe, meaning for the poor's benefit
one tenth, a tithe
to acquire on behalf of the poor

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
phrases.notes: This is a brand-new question, not the one from step 13. Now the field and the movables go to two different people.

phrases.english: A field to one person and movables to another, what is the law?
Come and hear:
The tenth that I will measure out in the future
is given to Akiva ben Yosef
so that he acquires it for the poor
and its place is rented to him.
What does 'rented' mean?
Rented for the tithe.
phrases.notes: The land was not rented for רבי עקיבא's own use. It was rented so the tithe would have a place for the poor.

steps.triggerLanguage: מאי מושכר מושכר למעשר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question after step 14 answered the previous one, brings a proof from the עקיבא part of רבן גמליאל's words, and rejects that proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from רבן גמליאל only
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The land and the tithe both went to the poor, so it is not a split deal.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא counts as the poor themselves
steps.stepSummary: A second rejection: רבי עקיבא was a charity collector, so he was like the hand of the poor. Giving to him is the same as giving to the poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: רבי עקיבא is different, because he was the hand of the poor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second, separate way to reject the proof from רבן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the land really was rented to רבי עקיבא, he was the charity collector, so he stands in for the poor. Then the land and the tithe went to one side after all. The original question stays without proof.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you want, say: an alternative answer
is different
the hand of the poor, a charity collector acting for them

steps.whatToRemember: Both rejections show that in רבן גמליאל's case everything went to one side. So the question of a field to one person and movables to another is not proven.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
Rabbi Akiva is different,
since he was the hand of the poor.
phrases.notes: He collected charity for the poor, so what he receives counts as theirs.

steps.triggerLanguage: ואי בעית אימא שאני רבי עקיבא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent rejection of the same proof.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי עקיבא was the same as the poor, so there were not two different receivers.

steps.title: Money acquires only as much as was paid
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that acquiring with money works for everything only if the buyer paid for all of it. Otherwise he acquires only what his money covers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: They taught this only when he paid the price of all of them. But if he did not pay for all of them, he acquires only as much as his money covers.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a new limit to the rule of acquiring things together with land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the deal is done with כסף, the money is what makes the buyer acquire. So if only part was paid, only that part is acquired, even if he took hold of everything.

keyTerms.meaning: they taught this only when
the price of all of them
matching his money, as much as he paid for

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the sale is cancelled. The buyer keeps what he paid for and does not acquire the rest.

phrases.english: Rava said:
They taught this only
when he paid the price of all of them,
but if he did not pay the price of all of them,
he acquires only as much as his money covers.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבא לא שנו אלא שנתן דמי כולן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the unsolved question and adds a new limit on acquiring through money.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With כסף, a buyer acquires only as much as he has paid for.

steps.title: A ברייתא agrees with רבא: money and document each have strengths
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is brought that agrees with רבא. It opens by listing how כסף is stronger than שטר and how שטר is stronger than כסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in agreement with רבא: Money is stronger than a document in one way, and a document is stronger than money in another way. Money is stronger, because money redeems הקדש and מעשר שני, which a document cannot do. A document is stronger, because a document releases a Jewish woman, which money cannot do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא that supports רבא. This part is the opening setup, and the part that matches רבא comes as the ברייתא continues.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא compares the two ways of acquiring. Only כסף can redeem holy items and מעשר שני. Only a שטר, a גט, can end a marriage. This comparison prepares the way for the point about money that supports רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in agreement with him
the power is stronger
things given to the Temple
second tithe
releases a Jewish woman, through a גט

phrases.english: It was taught in agreement with Rava:
The power of money is stronger than the power of a document,
and the power of a document is stronger than the power of money.
The power of money is stronger
because with money one redeems
consecrated property and second tithe,
which is not so with a document.
And the power of a document is stronger
because a document releases a Jewish woman,
phrases.notes: This means a גט, the document that ends a marriage.

phrases.english: which is not so with money.

steps.triggerLanguage: תניא כוותיה דרבא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support רבא's rule from step 17.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that money acquires only as much as was paid
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא comparing the strengths of כסף and שטר

steps.title: Money and document are stronger than taking possession
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues its comparison list. Both כסף and שטר are stronger than חזקה, because each of them can acquire an עבד עברי, and חזקה cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also, money and a document are each stronger than taking possession, and taking possession is stronger than each of them. How are money and a document stronger? Each of them can be used to acquire a Hebrew slave, but taking possession cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from step 18 keeps going with its comparison list. It now compares כסף and שטר with a third way of acquiring, חזקה, and first explains how כסף and שטר win.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 compared כסף and שטר with each other. Now a third method, חזקה, joins the list, and each side gets one advantage. Here כסף and שטר win, because an עבד עברי can be acquired with either of them but not with חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: Acquiring by taking possession, for example by working or improving a field
Has stronger power; is a stronger way to acquire in some respect
Both of them, meaning כסף (money) and שטר (document)
A Jewish servant who is sold for a fixed period of time

phrases.english: And the power of both of them is stronger
phrases.notes: 'Both of them' means money and a document, the two methods the ברייתא was just comparing.

phrases.english: than the power of taking possession,
and the power of taking possession is stronger than the power of both of them.
The power of both of them is stronger:
for both of them acquire a Hebrew slave,
phrases.notes: This goes back to what was taught earlier in the מסכתא (14b), that an עבד עברי is acquired with money or a document.

phrases.english: which is not so with taking possession.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיָפֶה כֹּחַ שְׁנֵיהֶם מִכֹּחַ חֲזָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא from step 18, adding חזקה to the comparison of כסף and שטר.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule in step 17 about acquiring with money in a deal that covers many items
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא comparing כסף, שטר, and חזקה

steps.title: Taking possession of one field acquires all ten
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives חזקה's advantage. If someone sold ten fields in ten different places, then once the buyer takes possession of one of them, he acquires all ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is taking possession stronger? If someone sold another person ten fields in ten different places, then as soon as the buyer takes possession of one of them, he acquires all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now explains the other side: how חזקה is stronger than כסף and שטר. Taking possession of just one field can acquire many fields at once, even fields that are far apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With חזקה, an act done on one field reaches all the other fields in the same sale, even if they are spread across different places. This is the part of the ברייתא that deals with one deal covering many items, which is exactly the situation רבא was ruling about in step 17.

keyTerms.meaning: Fields
Countries or regions, here meaning places far apart from each other
He took possession, meaning he did an act of חזקה
He acquired all of them

steps.confusionAlert: This line only teaches that חזקה on one field pulls in all the others. It does not yet say anything about whether the buyer paid. The connection to רבא's rule about payment comes in the continuation of the ברייתא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This 'one act acquires many fields' rule is the setting where the question of paying for everything versus paying for only part comes up. That is why this ברייתא is relevant to רבא's ruling.

phrases.english: The power of taking possession is stronger:
for with taking possession, if he sold him
ten fields in ten countries,
once he takes possession of one of them,
he acquires all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָפֶה כֹּחַ חֲזָקָה שֶׁחֲזָקָה מָכַר לוֹ עֶשֶׂר שָׂדוֹת בְּעֶשֶׂר מְדִינוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other half of the comparison started in step 19, this time explaining how חזקה is stronger.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule in step 17 about acquiring many items in one deal
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ten-fields clause of the ברייתא
